newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Edgy spot market keeps dollar vols firm.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Edgy spot market keeps dollar vols firm.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/pair options remained underpinned Tuesday despite a relatively quiet day in the spot market, dealers said.

The dollar is hovering around a pivotal level at 1.84 marks, and the possibility it could clear the hurdle and retest the recent highs is underpinning volatility, said an options trader for a U.S. bank. Dollar/mark reached a peak of 1.8913 marks on August 6.
"Traders are generally of the opinion that the move is not finished yet," the trader said.
There has been good two-way interest in dollar puts and dollar calls, though the market has been leaning toward dollar call purchases in dollar/mark, the trader continued.
Last week's volatile spot movements have left many options traders gunshy about selling options, said Masao Okada, chief dealer for Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank.
"It is too risky to be short vega or short gamma in this type of unstable situation," Okada said.

Market participants also were reluctant to sell volatility ahead of today's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which concluded with the U.S. central bank leaving key interest rates unchanged, traders said.
One-month dollar/mark volatility Tuesday afternoon was about unchanged from the previous session at 11.5/11.7 percent. Six-month and one-year vols were 11.5/11.6 percent.
One-month dollar/yen volatility was also little changed at 12.4/12.6 percent, with six-month and one-year options pegged at 12.65/12.75 percent.

Keen buying interest in longer-dated yen puts/dollar calls continues, and that is bolstering back-end volatility in dollar/yen, the traders said. Vols in the back end are garnering support from pressure on the yen that is related to the weakness in other Asian currencies, they said.
"Some speculators are trying to make the most of this situation in the back end," Okada said.
One-month 25-delta risk reversals were leaning 0.35/0.55 in favor of yen puts but were skewed slightly for mark calls at flat/0.2.
